\textbf{Main result}\par\medskip
The reported equations $\gamma c=-\ii s$ and $\gamma c=+\ii s$ do not define a physical no-go theorem.  The second sign is produced by mixing two different graded normal orders.  In either one consistent order, both derivations give
\[
\boxed{\gamma c=-\ii s}.
\]
Hence the linear invertible doublet/triplet package is viable; nonlinear or field-dependent packaging is not needed for this gate.

\section*{Notation and symbol dictionary}
\addcontentsline{toc}{section}{Notation and symbol dictionary}

本 note 先固定全部新记号。所有等式均在同一组 two-component spinor conventions 内解释。

\begin{definitionbox}[Two canonical graded normal orders]
For Grassmann-odd $\bar\zeta$ and $\chi$,
\begin{align}
\mathsf N_{\PL}\!\left(\bar\zeta\,\bar\sigma^\mu\cD_\mu\chi\right)
&=\bar\zeta\,\bar\sigma^\mu\cD_\mu\chi,
\\
\mathsf N_{\PR}\!\left(\bar\zeta\,\bar\sigma^\mu\cD_\mu\chi\right)
&=-(\cD_\mu\chi)\sigma^\mu\bar\zeta.
\end{align}
The minus sign is the Koszul sign
\[
(-1)^{\parity{\bar\zeta}\parity{\chi}}=(-1)^{1\cdot1}=-1.
\]
\end{definitionbox}

\section{What would a genuine obstruction mean?}

\subsection{The packaging map as an intertwiner}

Let $\mathcal F_{\N=1}$ denote the component field space written as one $\N=1$ vector plus one adjoint chiral multiplet. Let $\mathcal F_{SU(2)}$ denote the same off-shell degrees of freedom arranged into $SU(2)_R$ tensors. A linear package is a map
\[
P:\mathcal F_{\N=1}\longrightarrow\mathcal F_{SU(2)}.
\]
It is a valid $\N=2$ dictionary precisely when it intertwines every supersymmetry transformation:
\begin{equation}
P\,\delta_{\N=1}=\delta_{SU(2)}\,P.
\label{eq:intertwiner}
\end{equation}
Equivalently, the diagram commutes:
\[
\begin{CD}
\mathcal F_{\N=1} @>{P}>> \mathcal F_{SU(2)}\\
@V{\delta_{\N=1}}VV @VV{\delta_{SU(2)}}V\\
\mathcal F_{\N=1} @>{P}>> \mathcal F_{SU(2)}.
\end{CD}
\]

A genuine linear obstruction would mean that the coefficient equations following from \cref{eq:intertwiner} have no solution with
\[
\det P\neq0,
\qquad
sabc\neq0.
\]
Such a conclusion must be invariant under:
\begin{enumerate}
\item invertible field redefinitions;
\item rephasing of the $SU(2)_R$ basis;
\item a consistent change of graded monomial order;
\item Hermitian conjugation performed as an anti-automorphism.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection{Why a physical no-go is already implausible}

The standard rigid $4d\;\N=2$ vector multiplet is an irreducible finite off-shell $8+8$ representation with independent fields
\[
(X,\Omega_i,Y_{ij},W_\mu),
\qquad
Y_{ij}=Y_{ji},
\]
and a reality condition leaving three real components in $Y_{ij}$ \cite{VanProeyen1995}. Its off-shell counting is exact:
\begin{align}
N_B&=(4-1)_{W_\mu}+2_X+3_Y=8,
\\
N_F&=2\times4_{\text{two Weyl fermions}}=8.
\end{align}
Therefore the standard vector multiplet does not suffer from the finite-auxiliary-field problem familiar from a generic hypermultiplet. A contradiction found inside one $\N=1\to SU(2)_R$ dictionary must first be tested for convention consistency before it is interpreted as physics.

\begin{resultbox}[Classification of the reported result]
The current contradiction is not:
\begin{itemize}
\item a quantum anomaly;
\item a cohomological no-go theorem;
\item a proof that $\N=2$ SYM closes only on shell;
\item evidence that nonlinear packaging is required.
\end{itemize}
It is a false-positive coefficient residual generated by combining one parameter-left coefficient with one field-left coefficient.
\end{resultbox}

\section{The exact $\N=1$ sign identities}

\subsection{Chiral top-slot transformation}

With the project normalization
\[
\delta\phi=-\sqrt2\,\eps\psi,
\qquad
\delta\psi_\alpha=-\sqrt2\,\eps_\alpha F
+\ii\sqrt2\,\sigma^\mu_{\alpha\dot\alpha}\bar\eps^{\dot\alpha}\cD_\mu\phi,
\]
the chiral top slot in parameter-left order is
\begin{equation}
\boxed{
\delta F\slot_{\bar\eps}
=+\ii\sqrt2\,\bar\eps\bar\sigma^\mu\cD_\mu\psi.}
\label{eq:F-left}
\end{equation}
Because $\bar\eps$ and $\psi$ are both odd,
\begin{equation}
\bar\eps\bar\sigma^\mu\cD_\mu\psi
=-(\cD_\mu\psi)\sigma^\mu\bar\eps.
\label{eq:koszul-spinor}
\end{equation}
Hence the same transformation in field-left order is
\begin{equation}
\boxed{
\delta F\slot_{\bar\eps}
=-\ii\sqrt2\,(\cD_\mu\psi)\sigma^\mu\bar\eps.}
\label{eq:F-right}
\end{equation}
Equations \eqref{eq:F-left} and \eqref{eq:F-right} are identical statements. The coefficient changes sign because the monomial order changes.

\subsection{Vector auxiliary transformation}

The manifest vector-multiplet rule contains
\begin{equation}
\boxed{
\delta\mathscr D\slot_{\bar\eps}
=+\bar\eps\bar\sigma^\mu\cD_\mu\lambda
=-(\cD_\mu\lambda)\sigma^\mu\bar\eps.}
\label{eq:D-orders}
\end{equation}
Thus both the $F$ derivative slot and the $\mathscr D$ derivative slot acquire a minus sign under the same change from parameter-left to field-left order.

\subsection{Hermitian conjugation does not remove the ordering issue}

For homogeneous operators $X,Y$,
\begin{equation}
(XY)^\dagger=Y^\dagger X^\dagger.
\label{eq:dagger-anti}
\end{equation}
No Koszul sign is inserted into \cref{eq:dagger-anti}; the order is reversed. If one subsequently restores parameter-left order, the odd factors must be exchanged and one minus sign appears. For example,
\begin{align}
\left(+\ii\sqrt2\,\eps\sigma^\mu\cD_\mu\widetilde\psi\right)^\dagger
&=-\ii\sqrt2\,(\cD_\mu\psi)\sigma^\mu\bar\eps,
\\
&=+\ii\sqrt2\,\bar\eps\bar\sigma^\mu\cD_\mu\psi.
\end{align}
This is exactly \cref{eq:F-right,eq:F-left}. A sign audit that conjugates coefficients but forgets that the operator order reverses is incomplete.

\section{The $SU(2)_R$ package and the gaugino equations}

\subsection{General linear ansatz}

The gate uses
\begin{align}
\chi_1&=\psi,
&\chi_2&=s\lambda,
&\zeta^1&=\eps,
&\zeta^2&=s^{-1}\eta,
\label{eq:general-doublet}
\\
Y_{11}&=aF,
&Y_{22}&=b\widetilde F,
&Y_{12}&=Y_{21}=cH,
& H&=\mathscr D+\mu,
\label{eq:general-triplet}
\end{align}
with $sabc\neq0$. The auxiliary and moment-map part of the fermion transformation is
\begin{equation}
\delta\chi_i\slot_{Y,\mu}
=\gamma Y_{ij}\zeta^j+\beta\mu\eps_{ij}\zeta^j.
\label{eq:fermion-ansatz}
\end{equation}

\subsection{Manifest $F\eps$ slot}

For $i=1$, the $F\eps$ term in \cref{eq:fermion-ansatz} is
\[
\gamma Y_{11}\zeta^1
=\gamma aF\eps.
\]
The $\N=1$ chiral rule gives
\[
\delta\chi_1\slot_{F\eps}
=\delta\psi\slot_{F\eps}
=-\sqrt2\,F\eps.
\]
Therefore
\begin{equation}
\boxed{\gamma a=-\sqrt2.}
\label{eq:gamma-a}
\end{equation}

\subsection{Manifest $\mathscr D\eps$ gaugino slot}

For $i=2$,
\[
\delta\chi_2\slot_{\mathscr D\eps}
=s\,\delta\lambda\slot_{\mathscr D\eps}
=s(-\ii\eps\mathscr D)
=-\ii s\,\mathscr D\eps.
\]
The $Y$ term gives
\[
\gamma Y_{21}\zeta^1
=\gamma cH\eps
=\gamma c\mathscr D\eps+\gamma c\mu\eps.
\]
Comparing only the $\mathscr D\eps$ coefficient yields
\begin{equation}
\boxed{\gamma c=-\ii s.}
\label{eq:gaugino-c}
\end{equation}
This equation is independent of the monomial-order issue because $\mathscr D$ is bosonic.

\section{Forensic reconstruction of the false $+\ii s$}

The verifier stores transformation matrices in parameter-left order. In particular, it extracts
\begin{align}
\frac{A_{\PL}}{a}&=+\ii\sqrt2
&&\text{from }F\leftarrow\bar\eps\,\cD\psi,
\label{eq:stored-F}
\\
q_{\mathscr D,\PL}&=+1
&&\text{from }\mathscr D\leftarrow\bar\eps\,\cD\lambda.
\label{eq:stored-D}
\end{align}
The gate then manually converts only the second coefficient to field-left order:
\begin{equation}
q_{\mathscr D,\PR}=-q_{\mathscr D,\PL}=-1,
\label{eq:D-converted}
\end{equation}
but it leaves \cref{eq:stored-F} unchanged. It therefore combines
\[
\frac{A_{\PL}}a=+\ii\sqrt2
\qquad\text{with}\qquad
\frac{c}{A_{\PR}s}=-\frac12.
\]
These two ratios do not belong to the same coefficient system.

The resulting machine expression is
\begin{align}
\left.\frac{\gamma c}{s}\right|_{\text{mixed}}
&=(\gamma a)
\left(\frac{A_{\PL}}a\right)
\left(\frac{c}{A_{\PR}s}\right)
\\
&=(-\sqrt2)(+\ii\sqrt2)\left(-\frac12\right)
\\
&=(-2\ii)\left(-\frac12\right)
\\
&=+\ii.
\label{eq:false-plus-i}
\end{align}
The gaugino slot gives
\[
\left.\frac{\gamma c}{s}\right|_{\text{gaugino}}=-\ii.
\]
Thus the reported residual is
\begin{align}
\mathfrak O_{\text{mixed}}
&=\left.\frac{\gamma c}{s}\right|_{\text{triplet,mixed}}
-
\left.\frac{\gamma c}{s}\right|_{\text{gaugino}}
\\
&=(+\ii)-(-\ii)
\\
&=2\ii.
\end{align}
The residual is generated by the inconsistent normal-order change itself.

\begin{warningbox}[The exact logical failure]
The pair
\[
\frac{A_{\PL}}a=+\ii\sqrt2,
\qquad
\frac{c}{A_{\PR}s}=-\frac12
\]
cannot be multiplied as though $A_{\PL}=A_{\PR}$. They satisfy
\[
A_{\PR}=-A_{\PL}.
\]
The missing minus sign is the entire reported obstruction.
\end{warningbox}

\section{Correct derivation in parameter-left order}

Choose one canonical law:
\begin{equation}
\boxed{
\delta Y_{ij}\slot_{\cD\chi\bar\zeta}
=A_{\PL}\,\bar\zeta_{(i}\bar\sigma^\mu\cD_\mu\chi_{j)}.}
\label{eq:Y-left-law}
\end{equation}

\subsection{$Y_{11}$ slot}

From $Y_{11}=aF$ and \cref{eq:F-left},
\begin{align}
\delta Y_{11}\slot_{\bar\eps}
&=a\,\delta F\slot_{\bar\eps}
\\
&=a\left(+\ii\sqrt2\,\bar\eps\bar\sigma^\mu\cD_\mu\psi\right)
\\
&=a\ii\sqrt2\,\bar\zeta_1\bar\sigma^\mu\cD_\mu\chi_1.
\end{align}
Equation \eqref{eq:Y-left-law} gives
\[
\delta Y_{11}\slot_{\bar\eps}
=A_{\PL}\,\bar\zeta_1\bar\sigma^\mu\cD_\mu\chi_1.
\]
Therefore
\begin{equation}
\boxed{A_{\PL}=a\ii\sqrt2.}
\label{eq:AL-a}
\end{equation}

\subsection{$Y_{12}$ slot}

The manifest derivative in $H$ is
\[
\delta H\slot_{\bar\eps}
=+\bar\eps\bar\sigma^\mu\cD_\mu\lambda.
\]
Using $Y_{12}=cH$ and $\chi_2=s\lambda$,
\begin{align}
\delta Y_{12}\slot_{\bar\eps}
&=c\,\bar\eps\bar\sigma^\mu\cD_\mu\lambda
\\
&=\frac cs\,\bar\zeta_1\bar\sigma^\mu\cD_\mu\chi_2.
\end{align}
Equation \eqref{eq:Y-left-law} gives, with unit-weight symmetrization,
\begin{align}
\delta Y_{12}\slot_{\bar\eps}
&=\frac{A_{\PL}}2\,
\bar\zeta_1\bar\sigma^\mu\cD_\mu\chi_2.
\end{align}
Hence
\begin{equation}
\boxed{\frac{A_{\PL}s}{2}=c.}
\label{eq:c-AL}
\end{equation}

\subsection{Exact compatibility with the gaugino slot}

Using \cref{eq:gamma-a,eq:AL-a,eq:c-AL},
\begin{align}
\gamma c
&=\gamma\left(\frac{A_{\PL}s}{2}\right)
\\
&=\frac12\gamma A_{\PL}s
\\
&=\frac12\gamma(a\ii\sqrt2)s
\\
&=\frac12(\gamma a)\ii\sqrt2\,s
\\
&=\frac12(-\sqrt2)\ii\sqrt2\,s
\\
&=\frac12(-2\ii)s
\\
&=-\ii s.
\end{align}
Thus the symmetric-triplet slot gives exactly the same equation as \cref{eq:gaugino-c}:
\begin{equation}
\boxed{\gamma c=-\ii s.}
\end{equation}

\section{Equivalent derivation in field-left order}

The same law may be written as
\begin{equation}
\boxed{
\delta Y_{ij}\slot_{\cD\chi\bar\zeta}
=A_{\PR}(\cD_\mu\chi_{(i})\sigma^\mu\bar\zeta_{j)}.}
\label{eq:Y-right-law}
\end{equation}
Using \cref{eq:koszul-spinor},
\begin{equation}
A_{\PR}=-A_{\PL}.
\label{eq:ARminusAL}
\end{equation}
Equations \eqref{eq:AL-a} and \eqref{eq:c-AL} become
\begin{equation}
\boxed{
A_{\PR}=-a\ii\sqrt2,
\qquad
\frac{A_{\PR}s}{2}=-c.}
\label{eq:right-relations}
\end{equation}
Now compute without changing order midway:
\begin{align}
\gamma c
&=\gamma\left(-\frac{A_{\PR}s}{2}\right)
\\
&=-\frac12\gamma A_{\PR}s
\\
&=-\frac12\gamma(-a\ii\sqrt2)s
\\
&=\frac12(\gamma a)\ii\sqrt2\,s
\\
&=\frac12(-\sqrt2)\ii\sqrt2\,s
\\
&=-\ii s.
\end{align}
Both canonical orders therefore produce the same invariant coefficient.

\begin{resultbox}[Normal-order covariance]
The two valid systems are
\[
\left\{
\frac{A_{\PL}}a=+\ii\sqrt2,
\frac{c}{A_{\PL}s}=+\frac12
\right\},
\qquad
\left\{
\frac{A_{\PR}}a=-\ii\sqrt2,
\frac{c}{A_{\PR}s}=-\frac12
\right\}.
\]
Each system gives $\gamma c/s=-\ii$. The invalid mixed system takes the first entry from the left set and the second entry from the right set.
\end{resultbox}

\section{The corrected canonical $\N=2$ vector-multiplet dictionary}

Choose the project normalization
\begin{align}
\chi_1&=\psi,
&\chi_2&=-\lambda,
&\zeta^1&=\eps,
&\zeta^2&=-\eta,
\label{eq:canonical-doublet}
\\
Y_{11}&=-\sqrt2F,
&Y_{22}&=-\sqrt2\widetilde F,
&Y_{12}&=Y_{21}=\ii H.
\label{eq:canonical-Y}
\end{align}
Thus
\begin{equation}
(a,b,c,s,\gamma)=(-\sqrt2,-\sqrt2,\ii,-1,1).
\label{eq:canonical-coeffs}
\end{equation}
The derivative coefficient is
\begin{equation}
A_{\PL}=-2\ii,
\qquad
A_{\PR}=+2\ii.
\label{eq:canonical-A}
\end{equation}
The relevant auxiliary law can be written in either exact form:
\begin{align}
\delta Y_{ij}\slot_{\bar\zeta}
&=-2\ii\,\bar\zeta_{(i}\bar\sigma^\mu\cD_\mu\chi_{j)},
\label{eq:canonical-Y-left}
\\
&=+2\ii\,(\cD_\mu\chi_{(i})\sigma^\mu\bar\zeta_{j)}.
\label{eq:canonical-Y-right}
\end{align}

\subsection{Moment-map coefficient}

For the canonical choice, the complete auxiliary and moment-map part is
\begin{equation}
\boxed{
\delta\chi_i\slot_{Y,\mu}
=Y_{ij}\zeta^j-\ii\mu\eps_{ij}\zeta^j.}
\label{eq:canonical-fermion}
\end{equation}
Check $i=1$ explicitly. Since $\eps_{12}=-1$,
\begin{align}
\delta\chi_1\slot_{Y,\mu}
&=Y_{11}\zeta^1+Y_{12}\zeta^2
-\ii\mu\eps_{12}\zeta^2
\\
&=(-\sqrt2F)\eps+(\ii H)(-\eta)
-\ii\mu(-1)(-\eta)
\\
&=-\sqrt2F\eps-\ii H\eta-\ii\mu\eta
\\
&=-\sqrt2F\eps-\ii(\mathscr D+\mu)\eta-\ii\mu\eta
\\
&=-\sqrt2F\eps-\ii\mathscr D\eta-2\ii\mu\eta.
\end{align}
This is the manifest chiral $F$ slot plus the hidden $\mathscr D$ and moment-map slots.

For $i=2$, $\eps_{21}=+1$ and $\chi_2=-\lambda$:
\begin{align}
\delta\chi_2\slot_{Y,\mu}
&=Y_{21}\zeta^1+Y_{22}\zeta^2
-\ii\mu\eps_{21}\zeta^1
\\
&=(\ii H)\eps+(-\sqrt2\widetilde F)(-\eta)
-\ii\mu\eps
\\
&=\ii(\mathscr D+\mu)\eps+\sqrt2\widetilde F\eta-\ii\mu\eps
\\
&=\ii\mathscr D\eps+\sqrt2\widetilde F\eta.
\end{align}
Multiplying by $-1$ gives
\[
\delta\lambda\slot_{Y,\mu}
=-\ii\mathscr D\eps-\sqrt2\widetilde F\eta,
\]
which is exactly the manifest and hidden gaugino auxiliary rule.

\subsection{Reality and auxiliary action}

With $F^\dagger=\widetilde F$ and $H^\dagger=H$,
\begin{align}
(Y_{11})^\dagger
&=(-\sqrt2F)^\dagger
=-\sqrt2\widetilde F
=Y_{22}
=Y^{11},
\\
(Y_{12})^\dagger
&=(\ii H)^\dagger
=-\ii H
=-Y_{12}
=Y^{12}.
\end{align}
The auxiliary quadratic form is
\begin{align}
\frac14Y^{ij}Y_{ij}
&=\frac14\left(Y_{22}Y_{11}+Y_{11}Y_{22}-2Y_{12}Y_{12}\right)
\\
&=\frac14\left(
2\widetilde FF+2F\widetilde F-2(\ii H)(\ii H)
\right)
\\
&=\frac14\left(4\widetilde FF+2H^2\right)
\\
&=\widetilde FF+\frac12H^2,
\end{align}
where the adjoint trace and its invariant symmetric metric are understood. Thus the same canonical package satisfies the Lorentzian contour and the auxiliary action normalization.

\section{Concrete verifier repair}

\subsection{Minimal repair: stay parameter-left}

The existing matrix builder already stores supersymmetry parameters on the left. The safest repair is therefore to keep the gate in that same normal form.

\begin{lstlisting}[style=pythonstyle,caption={Parameter-left coefficient extraction for the repaired gate}]
# Existing exact handles, all in parameter-left normal form.
gamma_times_a = selected_coefficient("psi0", "F", "1e0", p_zero)
# gamma_times_a = -sqrt(2)

A_L_over_a = selected_coefficient("F", "psi0", "1b0", p_time)
# A_L_over_a = +i*sqrt(2)

Dlambda_parameter_left = selected_coefficient(
    "D", "lambda0", "1b0", p_time
)
# Dlambda_parameter_left = +1

c_over_A_L_s = Fraction(1, 2) * Dlambda_parameter_left
# c/(A_L*s) = +1/2

gamma_c_over_s_from_triplet = (
    gamma_times_a * A_L_over_a * c_over_A_L_s
)
# (-sqrt(2))*(+i*sqrt(2))*(+1/2) = -i

residual = (
    gamma_c_over_s_from_triplet
    - gamma_c_over_s_from_gaugino
)
# residual = (-i) - (-i) = 0
\end{lstlisting}

The line
\begin{lstlisting}[style=pythonstyle]
field_first_dlambda = -d_barepsilon_barsigma_dlambda
\end{lstlisting}
should not feed a product that still contains the parameter-left $F$ coefficient. Either delete that conversion from this gate or convert the $F$ slot at the same time.

\subsection{Dual-order regression test}

A strong verifier should prove that both normal orders agree:
\begin{lstlisting}[style=pythonstyle,caption={Order-covariance regression test}]
A_R_over_a = -A_L_over_a
c_over_A_R_s = -c_over_A_L_s

gamma_c_over_s_left = (
    gamma_times_a * A_L_over_a * c_over_A_L_s
)
gamma_c_over_s_right = (
    gamma_times_a * A_R_over_a * c_over_A_R_s
)

assert gamma_c_over_s_left == MINUS_I
assert gamma_c_over_s_right == MINUS_I
assert gamma_c_over_s_left == gamma_c_over_s_right
\end{lstlisting}
The two minus signs in the right-order product cancel exactly:
\begin{align}
(-\sqrt2)(-\ii\sqrt2)\left(-\frac12\right)
&=(+2\ii)\left(-\frac12\right)
\\
&=-\ii.
\end{align}

\subsection{Documentation repair}

The component note should choose one style and use it everywhere. The parameter-left style is closest to the current matrix implementation:
\begin{align}
\delta_1F\slot_{\bar\eps}
&=+\ii\sqrt2\,\bar\eps\bar\sigma^\mu\cD_\mu\psi,
\label{eq:doc-F-left}
\\
\delta Y_{11}\slot_{\bar\eps}
&=-2\ii\,\bar\eps\bar\sigma^\mu\cD_\mu\psi,
\label{eq:doc-Y11-left}
\\
\delta Y_{ij}\slot_{\bar\zeta}
&=A_{\PL}\bar\zeta_{(i}\bar\sigma^\mu\cD_\mu\chi_{j)},
\label{eq:doc-general-left}
\\
A_{\PL}&=a\ii\sqrt2,
\qquad
\frac{A_{\PL}s}{2}=c.
\label{eq:doc-relations-left}
\end{align}
If the note instead uses field-left style, it must write
\begin{align}
\delta_1F\slot_{\bar\eps}
&=-\ii\sqrt2(\cD_\mu\psi)\sigma^\mu\bar\eps,
\\
\delta Y_{11}\slot_{\bar\eps}
&=+2\ii(\cD_\mu\psi)\sigma^\mu\bar\eps,
\\
A_{\PR}&=-a\ii\sqrt2,
\qquad
\frac{A_{\PR}s}{2}=-c.
\end{align}
The old combination
\[
A=+a\ii\sqrt2,
\qquad
\frac{As}{2}=-c
\]
is precisely the forbidden mixed-order pair.

\section{Regression proof obligations}

After the patch, the following exact checks should be required before changing the PR status.

\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Canonical package check}
\[
(a,b,c,s,\gamma)=(-\sqrt2,-\sqrt2,\ii,-1,1),
\qquad
\frac{\gamma c}{s}=-\ii.
\]

\item \textbf{Order covariance}
\[
\left.\frac{\gamma c}{s}\right|_{\PL}
=
\left.\frac{\gamma c}{s}\right|_{\PR}
=-\ii.
\]

\item \textbf{Koszul involution}
\[
\mathsf N_{\PL}\!\left(\mathsf N_{\PR}(M)\right)=M
\]
for each bilinear containing one odd parameter and one odd field.

\item \textbf{Hermitian-conjugation consistency}
\[
(XY)^\dagger=Y^\dagger X^\dagger
\]
followed by canonical normal ordering must reproduce the conjugate component rule exactly.

\item \textbf{Free Abelian closure}
The existing zero residual must remain zero; the patch changes the presentation of one coefficient extraction, not the transformation matrix.

\item \textbf{Non-Abelian closure}
The existing covariant-jet checks must be rerun. The local sign repair is independent of compensators, but the full audit should still verify that no documentation change was copied incorrectly into the non-Abelian rules.

\item \textbf{Audit status}
Only after the focused and repository-wide tests pass should
\[
\texttt{BLOCKED\_OFFSHELL\_SU2\_R\_PACKAGING}
\]
be replaced by a passing status.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Why nonlinear packaging cannot be the first remedy}

Suppose one keeps the inconsistent pair
\[
A=+a\ii\sqrt2,
\qquad
\frac{As}{2}=-c.
\]
The contradiction then appears already in the free Abelian derivative slots. A nonlinear correction contains at least one additional field. It cannot alter a coefficient multiplying a term linear in one fermion and one constant supersymmetry parameter at zero background. A field-dependent redefinition also reduces to its linear Jacobian at the origin. Therefore neither option repairs this residual without first correcting the linear graded sign.

The logical order is:
\begin{equation}
\boxed{
\text{normalize monomials}
\;\longrightarrow\;
\text{solve the linear gate}
\;\longrightarrow\;
\text{test nonlinear completion}.}
\end{equation}
For the present gate, the first step already produces a solution.

\section{Conceptual interpretation}

\subsection{The obstruction residual is not convention invariant}

Define
\begin{equation}
\mathfrak O
=
\left.\frac{\gamma c}{s}\right|_{\delta Y}
-
\left.\frac{\gamma c}{s}\right|_{\delta\chi}.
\end{equation}
A genuine representation-theoretic obstruction would satisfy
\[
\mathfrak O\neq0
\]
after every consistent change of basis and every consistent graded normal-order map. Here one finds
\begin{align}
\mathfrak O_{\PL}&=(-\ii)-(-\ii)=0,
\\
\mathfrak O_{\PR}&=(-\ii)-(-\ii)=0,
\\
\mathfrak O_{\text{mixed}}&=(+\ii)-(-\ii)=2\ii.
\end{align}
Because only the mixed expression is nonzero, it is not an invariant of the supermultiplet. It is an invariant of an inconsistent bookkeeping choice, and therefore has no physical content.

\subsection{Why the other closure tests could still pass}

The full free-closure matrix uses one exterior algebra and one parameter-left ordering. Its coefficients therefore retain the correct Koszul signs. The specialized triplet gate steps outside that representation when it manually converts only the $\mathscr D\leftarrow\lambda$ handle to field-left form. This explains the otherwise surprising pattern:
\[
\text{free closure}=0,
\qquad
\text{triplet gate}\neq0.
\]
The two calculations were not evaluating the same normal-form system.

\subsection{Theoretical meaning in one sentence}

The Codex result means that the current \emph{implementation of the dictionary} fails to be a graded intertwiner; it does not mean that the $\N=2$ vector multiplet fails to possess an off-shell $SU(2)_R$-covariant realization.

\section{Final result}

\begin{resultbox}[Resolved coefficient system]
For any $\gamma\neq0$ and $s\neq0$, the relevant linear equations admit
\begin{align}
 a&=-\frac{\sqrt2}{\gamma},
& c&=-\frac{\ii s}{\gamma},
& A_{\PL}&=-\frac{2\ii}{\gamma},
& A_{\PR}&=+\frac{2\ii}{\gamma}.
\end{align}
The hidden $\widetilde F\eta$ slot gives
\[
b=-\frac{\sqrt2s^2}{\gamma}.
\]
The moment-map coefficient is
\[
\beta=\ii s.
\]
The project choice $\gamma=1$, $s=-1$ yields
\[
(a,b,c,s,\gamma,\beta,A_{\PL},A_{\PR})
=(-\sqrt2,-\sqrt2,\ii,-1,1,-\ii,-2\ii,+2\ii).
\]
Every displayed equation is invertible and satisfies $\gamma c=-\ii s$.
\end{resultbox}

The correct conclusion is therefore
\begin{equation}
\boxed{
\text{No off-shell }SU(2)_R\text{ obstruction exists in the declared linear package.}}
\end{equation}
The blocker should be treated as a graded-ordering bug in the note and verifier, patched in one canonical normal form, and then revalidated by the existing exact closure suite.

\section{Reference formulas from the standard off-shell multiplet}

In the conventions of Van Proeyen \cite{VanProeyen1995}, the Abelian vector multiplet is written as
\[
(X,\Omega_i,Y_{ij},W_\mu),
\qquad Y_{ij}=Y_{ji},
\]
with the relevant transformation structure
\begin{align}
\delta X&=\bar\epsilon^i\Omega_i,
\\
\delta\Omega_i
&=\not\!\partial X\,\epsilon_i
+\frac12Y_{ij}\epsilon^j
+\frac12\sigma_{ab}F^{-ab}\eps_{ij}\epsilon^j,
\\
\delta Y_{ij}
&=2\bar\epsilon_{(i}\not\!\partial\Omega_{j)}
+2\eps_{ik}\eps_{j\ell}\bar\epsilon^{(k}\not\!\partial\Omega^{\ell)}.
\end{align}
These phases and factors should not be copied directly into a different two-component convention. Their role here is structural: a symmetric real auxiliary triplet exists and closes the $4d\;\N=2$ vector multiplet off shell.
